theme: Future: will / going to / present continuous
rule_en: will = an instant decision or a prediction. going to = a plan/intention already decided, or a prediction from present evidence. Present continuous = a fixed arrangement with a time or place.
rule_bn: তাৎক্ষণিক সিদ্ধান্ত/ভবিষ্যদ্বাণী → will; আগে থেকে ঠিক করা পরিকল্পনা → going to; নির্দিষ্ট সময়সহ পাকা অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্ট → present continuous।

sessions.title: Spot the Error
sessions.instruction_en: Tap the wrong word, then choose the fix.

items.prompt_en: The build failed again — fine, I am going to restart the pipeline
items.explain_en: A decision made at the moment of speaking takes 'will', not the pre-planned 'going to'.

items.prompt_en: We will migrate the Salesforce org to the new API version next quarter; it's already approved
items.explain_en: An already-approved plan uses 'going to', while 'will' signals a spontaneous decision.

items.prompt_en: I will meet the client at 3 p.m. tomorrow, it's in my calendar
items.explain_en: A fixed arrangement with a set time uses present continuous 'am meeting', not 'will'.

items.prompt_en: Look at the memory graph — this service will crash any second
items.explain_en: A prediction based on present evidence you can see uses 'going to', not 'will'.

items.prompt_en: That deploy looks stuck — don't worry, I am going to help you
items.explain_en: An offer decided at the moment of speaking uses 'will', not 'going to'.

items.prompt_en: After the release, I will learn Apex testing properly; I've wanted to for months
items.explain_en: A pre-existing intention uses 'going to', whereas 'will' marks an on-the-spot choice.

items.prompt_en: The team is going to fly to Dublin on Monday; the tickets are booked
items.explain_en: A booked arrangement with a day uses present continuous ('is flying'), not 'going to'.

items.prompt_en: I think the new feature is going to probably ship late
items.explain_en: A general prediction with 'I think' and 'probably' naturally takes 'will', not 'going to'.

items.prompt_en: You raised a good point — I promise I am going to review your code tonight
items.explain_en: A promise made at the moment of speaking uses 'will', not 'going to'.

items.prompt_en: She is going to give her demo at 10 tomorrow; the room is reserved
items.explain_en: A reserved appointment with a set time uses present continuous ('is giving'), not 'going to'.

sessions.title: Choose & Fill
sessions.instruction_en: Tap the correct option or chip.

items.prompt_en: "The build just failed." "Don't worry, I ___ fix it right now."
items.explain_en: 'will' = an instant decision made at the moment of speaking, reacting to the failed build.

items.prompt_en: I ___ learn Apex this quarter; I've already signed up for the Trailhead course.
items.explain_en: 'going to' = a plan/intention already decided before speaking (the sign-up shows it).

items.prompt_en: We ___ the new feature to production at 9 a.m. tomorrow; the release is scheduled.
items.explain_en: Present continuous = a fixed arrangement with a set time (9 a.m. tomorrow).

items.prompt_en: Look at all these failing tests — this code ___ pass code review.
items.explain_en: 'going to' = a prediction based on present evidence (the failing tests you can see now).

items.prompt_en: "Who can demo the LWC?" "I ___ do it."
items.explain_en: 'will' = an instant decision to volunteer, made right now in response.

items.prompt_en: By 2030, AI ___ probably write most of our boilerplate code.
items.explain_en: 'will' is used for a general future prediction not based on present evidence.

items.prompt_en: I ___ the architects at 3 p.m. — the meeting is already on my calendar.
items.explain_en: Present continuous = a fixed arrangement with a definite time (3 p.m.).

items.prompt_en: She has decided she ___ apply for the senior developer role next month.
items.explain_en: 'going to' = an intention already decided ("has decided") before speaking.

items.prompt_en: The deploy log is full of red errors — this release ___ go smoothly.
items.explain_en: 'going to' = a prediction from present evidence (the red errors in the log now).

items.prompt_en: "My laptop just crashed!" "Okay, I ___ lend you mine."
items.explain_en: 'will' = a spontaneous, instant decision made in reaction to the crash.

sessions.title: Build It
sessions.instruction_en: Tap the tiles in the right order. For speak items, say it out loud.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: I will call you right back .
items.explain_en: Instant decision made at the moment of speaking, so 'will' fits here.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: We are going to refactor the API next sprint .
items.explain_en: 'going to' marks a plan already decided before speaking.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: The deploy is starting at 9 tomorrow .
items.explain_en: Present continuous shows a fixed arrangement with a set time.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: Look at the logs , the job is going to fail .
items.explain_en: 'going to' is a prediction based on present evidence (the logs).

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: I think this release will be smooth .
items.explain_en: After 'I think', use 'will' for a prediction or opinion.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: I'm meeting the client on Friday morning .
items.explain_en: Present continuous fits a fixed arrangement with a day and time.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: I am going to study for the Salesforce exam this weekend .
items.explain_en: 'going to' shows an intention you already decided on.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: Don't worry , I will fix the bug now .
items.explain_en: A willing decision made right now takes 'will', not 'going to'.

items.prompt_en: Say a sentence about a plan you already decided for your career using 'going to'.
items.model_en: I'm going to apply for a senior Salesforce developer role next month.

items.prompt_en: Say a sentence about a fixed work arrangement for tomorrow using the present continuous.
items.model_en: I'm presenting the demo to the team at 10 tomorrow.

sessions.title: Mixed Drill
sessions.instruction_en: All four types, shuffled. Beat the clock.

items.prompt_en: Look, the deploy bar is red — the build will fail
items.explain_en: Present evidence (the red bar) signals a prediction, so use 'going to', not 'will'.

items.prompt_en: I have decided it: I will refactor this Apex class tomorrow
items.explain_en: A decision already made before speaking takes 'going to', not the instant-decision 'will'.

items.prompt_en: The phone is ringing — that's the client. I am going to take it
items.explain_en: An instant decision made at the moment of speaking uses 'will', not the pre-planned 'going to'.

items.prompt_en: My flight to the conference ___ at 6 a.m. tomorrow, so I packed already.
items.explain_en: A fixed travel arrangement with a set time uses present continuous ('is leaving').

items.prompt_en: Don't worry about the merge conflict — I ___ help you resolve it.
items.explain_en: A spontaneous offer decided right now uses 'will'.

items.prompt_en: Look at those error logs piling up — the integration ___ break soon.
items.explain_en: A prediction based on present evidence (the logs) uses 'going to'.

items.prompt_en: We ___ the new release at 3 p.m. on Friday; the calendar invite is sent.
items.explain_en: A fixed arrangement with a set time and place uses present continuous.

items.prompt_en: I think our team ___ win the hackathon next month.
items.explain_en: A prediction or opinion with no present evidence uses 'will'.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: I am going to learn Salesforce Flow this weekend .
items.explain_en: A pre-made plan uses 'be going to' + base verb.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: I am meeting the recruiter on Monday morning .
items.explain_en: A fixed personal arrangement with a time uses present continuous.
